extracted.intended_audience: ship captains, pilots, shipping agents, and port officials calling at the Port of Buenos Ayres
extracted.subtask_description: Operational and legal rules for vessels arriving at and anchored in the Port of Buenos Ayres, covering signalling, health/quarantine procedures, communication restrictions, anchorage dues, and port police obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard ship signal on arrival (Article 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guard ship, in the inner roads, on observing a vessel anchor in the outer roads, will hoist a red flag at the mizen mast, as a signal to the captain of the vessel which has arrived, to proceed towards the shore in his boat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captain to present papers to guard ship (Article 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The said captain, taking with him his papers, will go on board the guard ship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure on boat arrival and health-visit signal (Article 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the arrival of the boat, the commandant of the guard ship will desire her to anchor astern, and will then hoist a yellow flag, for the health boat to come and pass the visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: No communication before health visit (Article 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The commandant of the guard ship must not permit any communication between his crew and those of the boat, until after the health visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health and war visit interrogation; penalties for false answers (Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The captain will be interrogated by the health and war visit; and if he does not answer truly, he will be tried by the laws of the country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weather exceptions and quarantine procedure (Article 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the weather will not permit the health-boat to pass the visit, the commandant of the guard-ship will wait till they make signals from the shore. If the weather be too boisterous and the boat cannot come on shore, the commandant may permit the crew to go on board him, and then the guard-ship herself will be considered in a state of quarantine, and must not communicate with any person until after the health visit has passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Striking flags after health visit (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the health visit has fulfilled her office, the commandant of the guard-ship will strike the red and yellow flags, mentioned in the Articles 1st and 3d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to communicate and port briefing (Article 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Having permission to communicate with the shore, captains will present themselves at the Captain of the Port's office, where they will fully inform him of the police of the port.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for entering Ensenada via Point Lara (Article 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: On arriving at the anchorage of Point Lara, captains who wish to enter the port of Ensenada, will hoist a flag at the mizen-mast, proceed to the vicinity of the fortress, and there wait the health and war visit. They are expressly forbidden to communicate with any person, under the penalties established by the quarantine laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for ships of war (Article 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ships of war are an exception; they are not required to conform to the above articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contagious disease on warships (Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: All ships of war, in which the crew may be attacked by a contagious disorder, will hoist a yellow flag, and be subject to the laws of quarantine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchorage dues for foreign vessels (Anchorage Dues)
rubrics_metrics.description: For foreign vessels, by the ton, four reals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dues (for foreign vessels) must be paid half on arrival, and half on departure; pilots' charges are included in anchorage dues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchorage dues for national vessels from foreign parts (Anchorage Dues)
rubrics_metrics.description: For national vessels, from foreign parts, two reals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dues must be paid half on arrival and half on departure; if a national vessel neither takes nor receives cargo it pays half the dues; national vessels pay half the health visit and certificate fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment timing for anchorage dues
rubrics_metrics.description: The dues mentioned must be paid, half on arrival, and half on the departure of the vessel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced dues for vessels not taking or receiving cargo
rubrics_metrics.description: National and foreign vessels, which neither take nor receive cargo, will only pay half the dues mentioned above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health visit and certificate fees for foreign vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign vessels will pay, besides, on their entry, twelve dollars for the health visit, and twelve dollars more upon their departure for the health certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health visit and certificate fees for national vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: National vessels only pay half for the visit and the health certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilotage charges included
rubrics_metrics.description: The charges for pilots are included in the anchorage dues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual assistance obligation (Police Article 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every vessel anchored in the port of Buenos Ayres must mutually render each other assistance, in case of drifting, or other risk of average. Those who refuse will be subject to the sentence and penalties prescribed by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for anchor buoys due to shallow water (Police Article 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is expressly enjoined to every vessel anchored in the port to have on its anchors correspondent buoys, as vessels coming in and going out, not seeing the buoys, run a risk of striking on the anchors. Those who fail using precaution in this respect will be responsible for the averages and losses that may result from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for vessels without buoys (Police Article 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vessels which have not buoys will give notice to the Captain of the Port, who will send some, with a pilot to place them. The anchor must not be raised without a permission to that effect.
